items: The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) filed a motion for the release of 216 individuals detained for over 36 hours after a mass arrest during a protest in Muntinlupa City.
NUPL argues that the detainees have not received any formal charges or evidence against them, violating their rights under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code.

MANILA, Philippines – The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) on Tuesday, November 17, filed a motion with the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor’s Office seeking the release of 216 people who have been detained for more than 36 hours following a mass arrest in Muntinlupa City.
In its motion, NUPL said those detained have yet to receive copies of any complaint-affidavit, witness affidavits, or other evidence supporting the charges against them.
Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code requires authorities to bring persons arrested without a warrant before judicial authorities within 12, 18, or 36 hours, depending on the gravity of the offense.
“The prolonged detention of the Respondents, absent the filing of a criminal case, constitutes a continuing violation of their fundamental rights,” NUPL said.

The lawyers asserted that the arrested individuals had not committed any criminal offense, saying many were merely exercising their constitutional rights to free speech, peaceful assembly, and to seek redress of grievances.
The individuals were arrested during a Pax Silica protest on the opening day of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila on Sunday, November 15. They are detained at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City.
There are also minors who were arrested and brought to Bahay Pag-asa Tunasan, Muntinlupa.

The protesters, mostly members of Lakbayan Timog Katagalugan, were heading to Liwasang Bonifacio to join other groups opposing Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump’s scheduled arrival in the country.
Trump arrived on Tuesday, November 17, for the ASEAN-US Special Summit and a state visit.
At Liwasang Bonifacio, police arrested another 11 people as tensions rose between officers and protesters.
Several groups questioned the massive arrest and called for the release of those arrested.

University of the Philippines Diliman’s Council Committee on National Programs and Policies urged the Philippine National Police to release those who detained. In a statement on Tuesday, UP said protesters who gathered in their campus were prevented by the police to join the protest in Manila.

“Contrary to its initial recommendation that mass actions be done only after the 49th ASEAN Summit and other related summits, the government should allow ongoing protests to continue. These are not sources of embarrassment as these show openness to opposing views and the tolerance of critical reportage,” UP said. – Rappler.com
